frozen_original.title: FBI Under Kash Patel Opens Investigations of Journalists Who Covered Trump Negatively
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, reports emerged that the FBI under Director Kash Patel had opened leak investigations targeting journalists and news organizations that had published critical coverage of Trump, including reporters at major outlets who had covered the Russia investigation, January 6, and Trump's business dealings. The investigations were framed as leak probes but were widely understood as a tool for identifying and intimidating journalistic sources within the government. Press freedom organizations including Reporters Without Borders and the Committee to Protect Journalists condemned the investigations as a systematic assault on press freedom. The use of FBI investigative resources to target journalists marked a significant escalation of the authoritarian playbook against a free press.

primary.title: Supplied Allegation of FBI Leak Probes Targeting Critical Journalists
primary.description_short: Supplied allegation: FBI leak probes targeted journalists critical of Trump
primary.description_medium: The supplied record alleges that the FBI under newly appointed director Kash Patel opened leak investigations in February 2025 against journalists and outlets critical of Donald Trump. It describes the action as a probe into sources behind coverage and alleges a chilling effect on the press. The packet verifies Patel's start date only; it does not establish the investigation, targets, or retaliatory motive.
primary.description_long: The supplied entry alleges that in February 2025 the FBI, under Kash Patel, opened leak investigations targeting journalists and news organizations because of critical coverage of Donald Trump. It describes the probes as searches for government sources behind reporting on the Russia investigation, January 6, and Trump's business dealings, and says press-freedom groups condemned the action. Those details remain allegations in the supplied record. The packet names no investigated journalist or outlet, case number, FBI announcement, court filing, or direct evidence tying an investigation to unfavorable coverage. The FBI's biography states that Patel became director on February 20, 2025, but that official record does not corroborate the alleged probes. Search results located later reporting about an internal FBI inquiry into leakers and a separate March leak-investigation announcement by the Director of National Intelligence; neither establishes this specific February FBI action or its asserted motive. The targets, date, scope, and press-group response remain unverified. This draft is internal only and cannot be published as fact.

frozen_original.title: Trump Tells Supporters Immigrants Are 'Not Human Beings' at Rally
frozen_original.synopsis: At a July 5, 2019 rally in Cincinnati, Ohio, Trump used rhetoric describing immigrants attempting to cross the southern border in dehumanizing terms, telling the crowd that they were 'not human beings' and that the country was being 'invaded.' Trump had built a pattern of using the language of infestation and animalization when describing immigrants — language that scholars of genocide and mass violence identified as consistent with preparatory rhetoric used historically to make violence against groups more psychologically accessible. Human rights organizations including the UNHCR condemned the dehumanizing characterizations. The rally rhetoric came during the same period as mass ICE raids and the family separation policy.
